questions.text: A tool publishes an outputSchema of type array. What should the client validate when consuming its complete result?

options.A: Only that the text summary sounds consistent with an array.
options.B: The structuredContent against that schema, including when isError is true.
options.C: Only object-valued results, because arrays must first be wrapped in a dict.
options.D: Only successful results, because isError waives the output contract.

questions.explanation: The published output schema commits every complete result to conforming structuredContent, including error outcomes. Structured content can be any JSON value.

questions.text: A descriptor proposes mirroring an api_key argument into an HTTP parameter header. What does this lesson’s admission policy require?

options.A: Accept it if the header uses Base64 encoding.
options.B: Accept it if the tool claims readOnlyHint=true.
options.C: Accept it but log the key so routing can be audited.
options.D: Reject the descriptor because sensitive parameters must not be mirrored.

questions.explanation: Encoding is not secrecy. The lesson rejects sensitive routing fields during admission to keep credentials out of intermediary-visible metadata.

questions.text: A pagination loop stops only when result.get("nextCursor") is None; otherwise it assigns cursor=result["nextCursor"]. The current page has nextCursor="". What happens?

options.A: The loop continues and sends the empty string unchanged as the next cursor.
options.B: The loop stops because an empty string is falsey.
options.C: The client increments the empty string into page number 1.
options.D: The client decodes the cursor and chooses a page size.

questions.explanation: The empty string is not None, so this explicit null check follows the opaque cursor unchanged instead of stopping on truthiness.
